terra.problem: The passage does not say people bowed to these idols.
The verse does not say the idols are standing in plain sight.
A heart going soft does not convey the fear expressed by hearts melting in this verse.
The oven-door comparison does not make the melting image clear or land as a joke.
Going to the same doors again and repeatedly redialing add prior and repeated attempts that the text does not mention.
The text does not mention help from Jerusalem; it does not say Egypt receives none.
Calling harsh the opposite of patient suggests the master is impatient, which the text does not say.
The passage does not say everything runs along the Nile or that everybody feels its drying. Nor does the rest of the message keep returning to the riverbed.
There is no water going anywhere overstates the passage; it also says Egypt's streams will trickle.
The text does not say the people who work the river feel its effects first.
Calling Assyria a mighty empire adds a fact outside the passage without a reference.
The explanation repeats that Egypt will acknowledge the LORD without adding a meaningful explanation, making it notably flat.
The text says people will travel between the lands and worship together, but does not say they walk the highway to worship.
Calling Assyria a mighty empire adds a fact outside the passage without a reference.
Calling fighting the usual story suggests a history of conflict between Egypt and Assyria that this passage does not state.
The earlier passage does not call Egypt and Assyria the LORD's enemies; Assyria is not mentioned until verse 23.
The blessing does not say Israel is not above either nation; it simply does not call Egypt or Assyria Israel's servants.
